newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian interbank rates steady on low supply.
newsitem.headline: Croatian interbank rates steady on low supply.

text.p: Croatian interbank rates remained stable on Monday amid a slight shortage of kuna funds, dealers said.
"As we expected, the pre-holiday and holiday spending depleted the bank accounts," a dealer told Reuters. Friday was a public holiday in Croatia.
Twenty deals worth 38.9 million kuna were struck in Monday morning trade. Most of it, 36.4 million, was call money granted at a steady 10.5 percent rate.
Two 30-day loans were struck at an unchanged 15 percent.
There was 13 million left on the supply and four on the demand side, but the bids could not be matched due to bank regulations.
The amount of money in banks' accounts fell to 350 million kuna on Thursday, and two banks levelled their shortfalls by borrowing two million kuna in overnight trade.
On Saturday the banks had only 284.3 million kuna on their accounts, and shortfalls totalled 12 million. They were met in overnight trade. -- Davor Huic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
